title: EPOG-JM: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Economic Policies (2027-2029)
organization: EPOG-JM consortium (Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in economics, EU-supported)
overview: Two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in economics focused on economic policies for the global transition. The application platform for the 2027-2029 cohort opens in October 2026; Erasmus Mundus scholarships and regional top-up scholarships (including for Sub-Saharan Africa) are awarded on this round.
program_dates: 2027-2029 cohort (two academic years); interviews March 2027, results end of March 2027
deadline_text: Application deadline: January 27, 2027, 13:00 Paris time (opening of the application platform: October 2026). A second call might be opened later for self-paying students.
funding_details: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: monthly allowance of EUR 1,400 during both academic years
Erasmus Mundus scholarship covers student tuition fees, including a health and accident insurance scheme (complete fee waiver)
Regional top-up scholarships under NDICI-Global Europe; Region 9 (Sub-Saharan Africa) lists 'Congo - Democratic Republic of the'
Travel costs are not described as covered by the scholarship
Without scholarship: EUR 1,000/year if personal income is below EUR 26,400/year, otherwise EUR 9,600/year
participation_fee: No application fee mentioned on the admission or tuition-fee pages
stipend: EUR 1,400 per month (Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders)
eligibility: Bachelor's or equivalent degree of 180 ECTS; economics degree, or another field with at least 24 ECTS in economics and 6 ECTS in statistics or econometrics
Bachelor's GPA of at least 70% of the maximum scale
English: CEFR C1 or more, TOEFL iBT 95 or more, or IELTS Academic 7.0 or more; proof due no later than June 10 (native speakers and holders of an all-English degree exempt)
Applicants who previously held an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for another
nationality_requirements: 'All applicants, wherever they come from, are eligible' for an EMJM scholarship
Regional top-up scholarships: Region 9 (Sub-Saharan Africa) includes 'Congo - Democratic Republic of the'
No more than 10% of scholarship holders may share a nationality (does not apply to regional top-ups)
education_requirement: Bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) with at least 24 ECTS in economics and 6 ECTS in statistics/econometrics if not an economics degree; GPA at least 70% of the scale
language_requirement: English C1 / TOEFL iBT 95 / IELTS 7.0, proof by June 10
documents_required: Online application form with attachments (not by email)
Passport copy matching the nationality applied with
application_process: Complete the online form at application.epog.eu and upload documents in the Attachments section
Interviews in March 2027; results end of March 2027
eligibility_reason: DRC nationals are eligible and listed for the Sub-Saharan Africa top-up. It depends on whether the business degree contains 24 ECTS of economics and 6 of statistics, on a grade of at least 70% of the scale, and on a C1/IELTS 7.0 English proof, none of which the profile records.
potential_issues: English proof at C1 / IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL 95 is required by June 10 and no test score is recorded
Economics and statistics credit requirement may not be met by a business administration degree
Travel and installation costs are not described as covered
benefits: Two-year joint master in economic policy across several European universities
EUR 1,400 monthly allowance and full fee waiver for scholarship holders
relevance_reason: Directly relevant to the profile's public-sector and policy-analysis interests, with strong funding, but the economics credit and C1 English requirements make access uncertain.
upfront_cost_risk: English test fee before the deadline; no application fee mentioned
action: Count the economics and statistics credits on the Licence transcript and convert the grade to a percentage; if both meet the thresholds, book an IELTS/TOEFL sitting and submit at application.epog.eu before 27 January 2027, 13:00 Paris time.
notes: Programme title in the EACEA catalogue: 'Economic POlicies for the Global bifurcation - Joint Master'.

title: American University in Cairo African Graduate Fellowship (Fall 2027)

program_dates: Fall 2027 start; up to five semesters and one intervening summer session
deadline_text: Graduate admission, Fall 2027: December 15, 2026 (early admission); April 1, 2027 (regular admission). Fellowship applications, Fall 2027: Cycle 1 from 22 December to 17 January; Cycle 2 from 6 April to 6 May. The admission page also says international applicants wanting early Fall decisions should apply by the preceding October 1.

Medical service and health insurance fees
A monthly housing allowance or University residence at the New Cairo campus

Admitted to an AUC graduate programme and meeting graduate admission requirements
